entries.q: What is the eligibility criteria regarding backlogs for placement registration?
entries.a:
According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies - Placements 2025-26 (Eligibility Criteria)**:

* **General Rule:** All final-year students having **3 or fewer backlogs** are eligible to register without restrictions.

* **Backlog Definitions:**
  * **July–Nov 2024 semester and before:** Any core course with a **U**, **W**, or an **I/blank** grade is considered a backlog.
  * **Jan–May 2025 semester:** Any core course with a **U** or **W** grade is considered a backlog.

* **Exceptions (Not counted as a backlog):** A course will **not** be considered a backlog if:
  * The student obtains an email from the course faculty providing written assurance that the course will be completed before graduation, **OR**
  * The student has registered for the course in the July–Nov 2025 semester.

entries.q: Can a student with more than 3 backlogs register for placements?
entries.a:
According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies - Placements 2025-26** (Eligibility Criteria section):

No, only final-year students having **3 or fewer backlogs** are eligible to register without restrictions. 

However, a course will **not** be counted as a backlog if:
* The student obtains written assurance via email from the course faculty stating that they will complete the course before graduation, **OR**
* The student has registered for the course in the July-Nov 2025 semester.

entries.q: How are core course backlogs defined for the July-Nov 2024 semester?
entries.a:
According to **Student Guidelines & Policies Placements 2025-26** (Section: *Eligibility Criteria*):

For the July-Nov 2024 semester and before, any core course with a **U**, **W**, or an **I/blank** grade is considered a backlog. 

However, a course in these categories will **not** be considered a backlog if:
* The student obtains an email from the course faculty providing written assurance that they will complete the course before graduation, **OR**
* The student has registered for the course in the July-Nov 2025 semester.

entries.q: What is the minimum credit requirement for BTech students to be eligible for placements?
entries.a:
According to the Student Guidelines & Policies Placements 2025-26 (Section: Eligibility Criteria):

The minimum credit requirement for BTech students to be eligible for placements without needing special approval is **300 credits**. If a student does not meet this requirement, they must obtain approval from the placement team.

entries.q: What minimum credits are required for Dual Degree students to register for placements?
entries.a: According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies - Placements 2025-26** (Section: *Eligibility Criteria*), Dual Degree students require a minimum of **418 credits** to register for placements without needing special approval from the placement team.

entries.q: How many minimum credits must an MTech student have to be eligible for placements?
entries.a:
According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies - Placements 2025-26** (Eligibility Criteria section), an MTech student must have a minimum of **73 credits**. 

If a student does not meet this requirement, they must get approval from the placement team.

entries.q: What is the minimum credit requirement for MBA and MSc students to appear for placements?
entries.a:
According to Student Guidelines & Policies Placements 2025-26 (Eligibility Criteria), the minimum credit requirements are:

* **MSc**: **78 credits**
* **MBA**: **111 credits**

*(Note: If a student's total credits do not meet these minimum requirements, they must obtain approval from the placement team.)*

entries.q: Can a student on academic extension register for placements on Day 1 Slot 1?
entries.a:
According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies - Placements 2025-26** (Section: *Eligibility Criteria - Special Cases*):

* **Yes, if they have NOT appeared for Placements before:** A student on Academic Extension who did not appear for placements previously can appear from **Day 1 (Slot 1)**. They must submit relevant proof to the Placement Office and pay the Placement Registration fee.
* **If they HAVE appeared for Placements before:** The slot from which they can appear is **To Be Decided (TBD) by the Advisor**. They must submit relevant proof to the Placement Office, proof of graduation in 2026, and pay the Placement Registration fee.

entries.q: Can I participate in Day 1 Slot 1 if I deferred placements in the previous academic year?
entries.a:
According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies Placements 2025-26 (Section: Eligibility Criteria - Special Cases)**, **yes**, you can participate from **Day 1 (Slot 1)**, depending on your situation:

* **If you did NOT appear in any placement test or PPT in the past academic year:**
  * **Eligibility:** Allowed to appear from **Day 1 (Slot 1)**.
  * **Required Action:** Provide proof of approval of your deferral request from the previous year and pay the Placement Registration fee.

* **If you appeared in test(s) and/or PPT(s) before deferring:**
  * **Eligibility:** Allowed to appear from **Day 1 (Slot 1)** upon provision and approval of a valid excuse for why you deferred after participating.
  * **Required Action:** Provide proof of approval of your deferral request from the previous year and pay the Placement Registration fee.

entries.q: What happens if a student appeared for Phase 1 interviews in the past year but received no offer?
entries.a:
According to the **Student Guidelines & Policies Placements 2025-26** (Section: *Eligibility Criteria - Special Cases*):

A student who appeared for Phase 1 interviews in the past academic year and did not receive a job offer:
* **Can appear for placements starting from:** **Day 4**
* **Required Actions:** 
  * Inform the placement office and your department team.
  * Pay the Placement Registration fee.
